Choose the form that matches your situation. Required fields are marked with an asterisk (*).
Which form should I use?
Payment recovery: a transfer that has already completed and that you started yourself. See Recovering a completed transfer.
Mistaken transfer: you started the transfer but sent it to the wrong recipient or for the wrong amount.
Unauthorized transfer: you did not start the transfer. See Unauthorized transfers.
You can also reach us by phone at 1-800-555-0142 (a fictional number), 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. ET, or by email at support@northstar-mock.example. Do not send passwords or full account numbers.
Payment recovery request
Ask us to try to recover money from a completed transfer. Recovery is not guaranteed.
Report a mistaken transfer
Tell us about a transfer you started by mistake. A report creates a record and starts outreach; it is not a recovery request.
Report an unauthorized transfer
Use this only for a transfer you did not start and did not give anyone permission to start.

pages.title: Canceling a transfer | Northstar Mock Bank (simulated)

blocks.text: Canceling a transfer
What you can do with a transfer depends on where it is in its journey and how it was sent.
Most transfers move through three stages: Scheduled, Processing and Completed. You can see the current stage, and the time the next stage begins, on the transfer details page.
Scheduled transfers

A scheduled standard transfer may be canceled from its transfer details page at any time before processing begins. The details page shows the exact time under Processing starts. Once you confirm, the transfer is marked Canceled and no money leaves your account.
After processing has begun

Once a transfer is processing, it can no longer be canceled online. A completed transfer can't be directly canceled at all, because the money has already been delivered to the recipient. If you sent money to the wrong person or for the wrong amount, you may be able to ask us to try to get it back. See Recovering a completed transfer.
We check the transfer when you confirm

Cancellation depends on the state of the transfer at the moment you confirm, not at the moment you opened the page. If processing started while the page was open, we'll decline the request and leave the transfer unchanged. Reload the page to see the current status.
Some transfer types have their own rules

The guidance on this page describes standard transfers. It is general guidance and doesn't override rules that apply to a specific transfer type. In particular, instant transfers follow the exception described in Instant transfers, even when the transfer details page shows a Scheduled or Pending status.
Finding out which type of transfer you sent

The Payment method on the transfer details page shows whether a transfer is Standard or Instant. If it says "Not shown for this transfer", check the confirmation email you received when you sent it, or contact support, before relying on the guidance on this page.

blocks.text: Instant transfers
Instant transfers arrive within minutes. That speed is also why they follow different rules.
Instant transfers deliver money to the recipient's account within minutes, at any hour. They are designed for situations where speed matters.
Instant transfers can't be canceled

An instant transfer can't be canceled once it has been submitted. While the transfer is queued with the receiving bank, the transfer details page may briefly show a Pending or Scheduled status. That status describes queueing only; it does not mean the transfer can still be stopped, and the Cancel transfer button may still appear during that time. Any cancellation attempt will be declined.
This exception applies even though the general guidance in Canceling a transfer says scheduled transfers may be canceled.
If you sent an instant transfer by mistake
Wait until the transfer shows Completed, then follow the steps in Recovering a completed transfer. Recovery isn't guaranteed.
Not sure which type you sent?
The Payment method on the transfer details page shows Standard or Instant. If it isn't shown, your confirmation email lists the transfer type.

pages.title: Recovering a completed transfer | Northstar Mock Bank (simulated)

blocks.text: Recovering a completed transfer
A completed transfer can't be canceled, but in some cases we can ask the recipient's bank to return the money.
When a transfer has completed, the money is already in the recipient's account. We can't undo it directly. What we can do is submit a recovery request, which is separate from cancellation.
Is recovery guaranteed?

No. A completed transfer may be eligible for a recovery request, but the outcome depends on the recipient's bank and on the recipient. The money may already have been spent or moved. We'll email you the outcome of your request.
Which transfers are eligible

the transaction reference number, which appears on the transfer details page and in your confirmation email;
the recipient's information: their full name, their bank, and the last four digits of their account number; and

Complete the Payment recovery form on the Support page.

Report a mistaken transfer. If you don't have the reference number, or you only want us to notify the recipient's bank, use the Report a mistaken transfer form on the Support page. Ask the recipient. You can contact the recipient yourself and ask them to send the money back, using contact details you already have. We can't do this on your behalf.

rules.reviewReason: Recovery is explicitly not guaranteed (outcome depends on the recipient's bank and recipient); this warning cannot be represented as a condition, so eligibility does not imply a successful recovery.

citations.excerpt: A transfer that you didn't start or authorize is not a mistaken transfer. Don't use the recovery or mistaken transfer forms for it. Follow the separate process described in Unauthorized transfers.
We can't open a recovery request without the reference number and the recipient's information.
the transaction reference number, which appears on the transfer details page and in your confirmation email;
a short description of what happened and an email address where we can reach you.
Wait until the transfer shows Completed, then follow the steps in Recovering a completed transfer. Recovery isn't guaranteed.
